reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify potential spurious patterns in the feature values of misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and validate shared attributions. This approach ensures both pattern recognition and statistical validation of spurious feature influence across all misclassifications.

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the feature values of instance 541 and instance 128 to identify any shared high-value or outlier-like features that may be spurious
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that have similar or extreme values in both instances, particularly those that may not semantically relate to malignancy

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any of the shared features (e.g., mean concavity, compactness) are known to correlate with benign or malignant classes in medical literature and whether such correlations are spurious or context-dependent
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A judgment on the semantic relevance of the shared features to cancer classification

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP identifies high-impact features in a game-theoretic way, helping to detect which features are driving predictions despite being semantically unrelated. LIME provides local interpretability, confirming which features dominate prediction in specific instances. Integrated Gradients offer a global attribution score, highlighting features with disproportionate influence. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature causes significant prediction changes, indicating spurious dependency. Together, these tools validate shared, high-attribution features that may be spurious.
